finalText:
I have all the evidence needed. Here's the diagnosis:

---

## Diagnosis: Pod `c032-pending` — Unschedulable due to impossible GPU request

### Root Cause
The pod requests **999 GPUs** (`nvidia.com/gpu: 999`), but no node in the cluster has anywhere near that capacity. The maximum any single node provides is **8 GPUs**.

### Evidence

| Finding | Detail |
|---|---|
| Pod GPU request | `Requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 999` (also Limits: 999) |
| Max node GPU capacity | 8 GPUs per GPU-capable node (confirmed across `fake-node-*`) |
| Scheduler event | `5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` — only 5 nodes were even evaluated for GPU resources before rejection |
| Other nodes filtered | 357 of 368 nodes eliminated by taints (control-plane, kwok fake, unreachable) or marked unschedulable |

The scheduler correctly rejects every node — the 5 GPU-capable nodes each have 8 GPUs max, which is far below the requested 999.

### Impact / Scope
Limited to this single pod only. No other workloads are affected.

### Confidence
**High** — the resource request (999) objectively exceeds the maximum per-node supply (8). This is a configuration error, not a cluster health issue.

### Safe Remediation
Reduce the pod's GPU request to a realistic value matching the workload's actual needs (e.g., `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` or up to `8` for multi-GPU jobs). This requires editing the pod spec or its parent controller — which I cannot do read-only, but the fix is a simple parameter change.

toolCalls.args: {"command":"kubectl get pod c032-pending -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602 -o wide --cluster cks-test","cluster":"cks-test"}

{"command":"kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/worker --field-selector spec.unreachable=false -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ALLOCATABLE_GPU:.allocatable.'nvidia\\.com/gpu' 2>/dev/null || kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ALLOCATABLE_GPU:.allocatable.'nvidia\\.com/gpu',STATUS:.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status 2>/dev/null | head -20","cluster":"cks-test"}

{"command":"kubectl get nodes --no-headers -o custom-columns=\"NAME:.metadata.name, GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia\\.com/gpu, READY:.status.conditions[?(@.type==Ready)].status\" 2>/dev/null | grep -i gpu | head -10","cluster":"cks-test"}

{"command":"kubectl get nodes -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.allocatable[\"nvidia.com/gpu\"] != null) | \"\\(.metadata.name) gpu=\\(.status.allocatable[\"nvidia.com/gpu\"]) ready=\\(.status.conditions[] | select(.type==\"Ready\") | .status)\"' | head -10","cluster":"cks-test"}

## Diagnosis: Pod `c032-pending` — Unschedulable due to impossible GPU request

### Root Cause
The pod requests **999 GPUs** (`nvidia.com/gpu: 999`), but no node in the cluster has anywhere near that capacity. The maximum any single node provides is **8 GPUs**.

### Evidence

| Finding | Detail |
|---|---|
| Pod GPU request | `Requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 999` (also Limits: 999) |
| Max node GPU capacity | 8 GPUs per GPU-capable node (confirmed across `fake-node-*`) |
| Scheduler event | `5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` — only 5 nodes were even evaluated for GPU resources before rejection |
| Other nodes filtered | 357 of 368 nodes eliminated by taints (control-plane, kwok fake, unreachable) or marked unschedulable |

The scheduler correctly rejects every node — the 5 GPU-capable nodes each have 8 GPUs max, which is far below the requested 999.

### Impact / Scope
Limited to this single pod only. No other workloads are affected.

### Confidence
**High** — the resource request (999) objectively exceeds the maximum per-node supply (8). This is a configuration error, not a cluster health issue.

### Safe Remediation
Reduce the pod's GPU request to a realistic value matching the workload's actual needs (e.g., `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` or up to `8` for multi-GPU jobs). This requires editing the pod spec or its parent controller — which I cannot do read-only, but the fix is a simple parameter change.
